results.text: Methodology.SQL2NL (i) ingests a gold SQL query and its schema description; (ii) prompts a generation model with constraints that encourage lexical and syntactic diversity while forbidding schemaidentifier leakage; (iii) validates paraphrase fidelity through automatic embedding-based checks and targeted human review of a sample; and (iv) evaluates NL-to-SQL systems by comparing execution accuracy on the original questions with that on the SQL2NL paraphrases. The framework supports weighted (human-adjusted) scoring so that low-quality paraphrases do not unduly penalize systems. SQL2NL can also produce augmented training data for robustness-oriented fine-tuning. Evaluation protocol and datasets.The authors apply SQL2NL to Spider and BIRD and stratify their analyses by query complexity (number of joins, nested clauses, and aggregates). The primary metrics are execution accuracyand therobustness gap, defined as the drop in execution accuracy from the original to the paraphrased questions.

results.text: 4.3 Evaluating Robustness via SQL2NL: Schema-Aligned Paraphrasing The SQL2NL framework [69] proposes a schema-aware approach to measure and improve therobustness of NL-to-SQL systems under lexical and syntactic variation. Rather than paraphrasing natural language questions naïvely (which can inadvertently change schema links), SQL2NL generates paraphrases conditioned on thegold SQLand the target database schema, producing diverse utterances that preserve the original intent while keeping schema alignment intact. This makes it possible to measure how sensitive a model is to wording, independently of schema-linking errors.

results.text: – Schema-link agreement:compare the extracted schema links (tables, columns, constants) across samples to estimate whether the model consistently targets the same schema elements. • Trade-off.Black-box consistency is straightforward to apply to closed APIs, but its quality depends on the sample size and the chosen proxy (execution is the most reliable; embedding and schema proxies are cheaper). White-box logit aggregation.When token probabilities or logits are available, confidence can be constructed from the model’s internal scores by aggregating over semantically meaningful token sets: • Full-Token Confidence (FTC).Aggregates probabilities over all output tokens (by averaging or multiplication). FTC is simple but treats all tokens equally and can be dominated by syntactic tokens. • Schema-Linked Confidence (SLC).Restricts aggregation to schema-relevant tokens (table names, column names, and constants), focusing the score on the tokens that most directly affect semantic correctness.

results.text: (TSED). These metrics quantify both clause-level accuracy and the structural fidelity of predicted queries with respect to reference queries. SQL Query Analysis Metric (SQAM).SQAM decomposes each SQL query into its principal clauses: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY , HAVING, and ORDER BY . For every clause, the overlap between the predicted and reference sub-clauses is measured with precision, recall, and a weighted F1 score; semantically important clauses such as SELECT and WHERE receive higher weight in the final aggregation. In contrast to string-based metrics such as BLEU, SQAM penalizes omitted predicates, incorrect join conditions, and inappropriate aggregation choices, and therefore provides a more informative signal of partial correctness. Tree Similarity of Editing Distance (TSED).TSED compares the abstract syntax trees (ASTs) of the generated and reference queries.

Both queries are parsed into trees, and an edit distance is computed over node insertions, deletions, and substitutions; this distance is normalized by the size of the larger tree and converted into a similarity score in [0,1] (e.g., 1−normalized distance ). Because it operates on the AST, TSED captures hierarchical and structural similarity and rewards outputs that are structurally correct even when superficial token ordering or aliasing differs. Empirically, TSED correlates strongly with execution accuracy and is therefore a useful proxy when direct execution against the target database is not possible. Practical significance.SQAM and TSED form a complementary evaluation framework: SQAM focuses on clause-level and compositional correctness, whereas TSED captures global structural alignment. Used jointly, they provide a more robust assessment of model quality than either alone.

results.text: MAC-SQL.MAC-SQL [ 80] proposes a multi-agent collaborative pipeline comprising three agents: aSelector, aDecomposer, and aRefiner. The Selector filters the schema to retain only relevant tables and columns, reducing token overhead; the Decomposer applies chain-of-thought reasoning to break complex questions into sub-problems; and the Refiner executes candidate queries, collects errors or empty results, and iteratively fixes the outputs using this feedback. The framework is instantiated with GPT-4 for maximum accuracy and with SQL-Llama (Section 5.3) for open-source deployment. MAC-SQL set a new state of the art on BIRD at the time of publication (59.59% execution accuracy on the test set) and is competitive on Spider; its ablations show that each agent contributes to performance, confirming the value of multi-agent collaboration and error recovery. 24

Pass@Kis also reported to quantify latent capability under sampling. Key results.Experiments reveal substantial robustness deficits: large models exhibit notable executionaccuracy drops on paraphrases (around 10 percentage points for LLaMA-70B), and smaller models show even larger relative declines. Degradation increases with query complexity, with multi-join and nested queries being the most vulnerable. Pass@K recovers part of the gap but is not a practical substitute for single-shot robustness in production. Implications.SQL2NL is both a diagnostic and a data-generation tool: as a diagnostic, it exposes brittle lexical generalization that standard benchmarks hide; as a data source, it provides schema-aligned paraphrases for targeted fine-tuning that mitigates this brittleness. 10

A further, and often overlooked, threat to validity is the quality of the benchmarks themselves: recent expert audits report annotation errors in more than half of the examined instances of BIRD Mini-Dev and Spider 2.0-Snow, enough to change both reported accuracies and leaderboard rankings [ 39, 40]. • Spider 2.0[ 46]: a next-generation evaluation framework of 632 real-world enterprise workflow problems that extends the canonical Spider task toend-to-end problem solvingover relational databases. Spider 2.0 is designed to reflect realistic analytical workflows: it evaluates not only single-shot NL→SQL parsers but also multi-stage pipelines and autonomous agents that inspect schemas, issue exploratory queries, validate execution, and repair errors. Two derived settings,Spider 2.0-Lite andSpider 2.0-Snow, isolate the pure Text-to-SQL component.
